scope: Owner-commissioned deterministic-rig pilot for Roshan's wave with LTX animation as the motion guide, run as two tests at the owner's request. LTX Union take 1 is tracked (numbers only) and solved onto one fixed-length rig. Run 1 deliberately ignores the whole-frame, whole-sprite, no-Roshan-rig and written-handoff rules (owner-permitted test): a standalone Godot 4.7.2 Skeleton2D rig with skinned approved parts, rendered and measured. Run 2 restores the rules: proportion-locked structural guides (W3 lengths, one master phase) for the next whole-frame LTX take, plus an untested controlled-comparison runner. No game file, runtime path or finding lifecycle changes. Revision 2 of run 1 (owner review 2026-10-07, ODR-RIG-PILOT-REV2-20261007): the LTX arm path is smoothed, whole-body acting, underwater idle, hair flow and a pilot-only painted blink are authored on the LTX timing, and rig edge artifacts are repaired. Revision 3 (owner rejected revision 2: overdraw, figure not moving as a whole, rough crops; ODR-RIG-PILOT-REV2-REJECTED-20261007): run 1 is closed as evidence. Under "Continue, trial methods until satisfied" (ODR-RIG-PILOT-TRIALS-20261007) the run-2 takes run on the owner's RTX 3060 Ti through a PC job runner (ComfyUI graphs only, input hashes, node allow-list, 8-take cap counting failures) fed through the connected folder; jobs a1 (rig guides only) and a2 (plus frame-40 lock and finger sentence) are queued. Because the owner made outfit compatibility critical (ODR-RIG-PILOT-COSMETICS-20261007), whole-frame clips now flow into the game's outfit system: clip_cells.py maps take frames to 256 px cells, clip_pose_fit.py writes a constant-size, bodice-tracked pose fit, and tools/build_fashion_outfits.gd gains an opt-in --fit/--out mode that bakes ribbon, party, garden and disguise onto any clip atlas (default game outputs byte-identical). Proven on Union take 1 frames. Revision 4: all 8 local takes ran (a1, a2, c1, d2, d1, e1, f1, g1). Guides gained whole-outline acting (render_guides_acting.py), optional arm occlusion and authored arm paths (animate_run5.py, animate_run6.py with --run7); takes e1 to g1 shift the opening image and guides 40 px right. Every take is measured (W2, arm range, eye openness, end frames) and dressed in all four game outfits through the same pipeline; g1 is the best candidate (constant size, whole body moving, eyes open, crisp wave) with two open defects: a soft hand in about 11 rise and lowering frames and no blink. clip_cells.py gains an optional whole-clip colour match to K0 (--grade-to-k0), applied to g1. The take budget is spent; nothing is runtime or delivery.

acceptance_gaps: Run 1 is closed: the owner rejected revision 2 (overdraw, figure not moving as a whole, rough crops), and as a rules-off test it was never eligible for production under ODR-SPRITE-WHOLE-UNIT-20261007 and ODR-ROSHAN-WHOLE-FRAME-20261005. Run 2 spent its 8-take budget; the best candidate g1 still has a soft hand in about 11 frames, no blink, and no per-segment W3 proof, and is not deliverable without owner review and, for more takes, owner authorization. No approved front-facing closed-eye drawing exists. The outfit clips are reference-only (no runtime atlas, FashionDesigner.SOURCES entry or pose_fit.json change); owner art review of outfits in motion, the garment's whole-pixel slip (<= 0.66 px) and non-rotation are open. Mobile renderer, device, child and runtime gates are outstanding. MA-ROSHAN-006 and MA-VIS-008 lifecycles are unchanged.

lessons.lesson: A fixed-length rig solved from LTX footage holds Roshan's size exactly (figure 0.05%, head 0.16%) and is cheap, but as runtime art it reintroduces part layers and an arm that moves alone; use it to author proportion-locked guides, not as the delivered sprite.
Measure the guide family before generating: the Union take-1 guides themselves asked for the forearm to change from -62% to +41% of the contract, and the take followed them.
When rendering Godot animations frame by frame, set the AnimationPlayer to manual callback mode before seeking; a paused player still advances during the frame and shifts every capture.

Do not copy noise-level body motion or per-frame solves from generated footage onto a rig: smooth the LTX path (weighted by fit confidence) and author secondary motion on its timing, or the rig reads as frozen and jittery at once.
Overlay parts cut from one drawing must exclude neighbouring materials (hair in a sleeve overlay) and joint pivots must sit inside the covering part, or skinned motion exposes cuts and blobs.

A cut-out or skinned rig cannot meet whole-sprite acting: overlapping parts overdraw, each part turns about its own pivot, and moving a limb uncovers pixels the drawing never had. Keep rigs for guides and measurement.

Animation clips get outfits through the same per-cell builder as static atlases, but the bodice box must keep one size and only move with the tracked bodice; per-cell measured boxes would make clothing breathe.

LTX-2.5 packs 8 frames into one latent frame and the hand is about one latent token at 320x448: a hand moving across hair or face inside one group decodes as a smudge. Route the hand over plain background (a side wave) before trying prompts or occlusion; lowering the peak speed by a quarter did not clear the fastest frames.

Asking LTX for a blink, even a one-frame blink at a named frame, shut Roshan's eyes for 11 to 26 frames in all three takes that asked; takes that did not ask kept the eyes open. A short blink needs an approved closed-eye keyframe, not prompt text.
The connected-folder copy adds a C2PA chunk to PNGs; hash-gated runners must be given the hash of the copy actually on the PC after a pixel check, and re-sent files need fresh staging paths.
